scope: Theorem 7.1 (One-rate passage packets) of the manuscript “Uniform bounds for planar polynomial limit cycles” (preprints/uniform-bounds-for-planar-polynomial-limit-cycles-September-24-2026/uniform-bounds-for-planar-polynomial-limit-cycles-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 143 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8ff8e55372a94e4f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 90. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The following two passage outputs satisfy the packet conditions of Definition 3.1 and the differentiated primitive conditions of Assumption 4.2. 1. A regular base flow with endpoint layers, zs = V (s, z) + qW(s, E, H, z), W(s, 0, 0, z) = 0, Eν = eνe−aν qs , Hν = dνe−bν q(1−s) . (7.1) The weights are positive multiples of a fixed charge unit, and the amplitudes are sufficiently small. The base flow from the chosen input disk is analytic and regular throughout [0, 1], with room for a small perturbation. 2. A stable linear generator with bounded slow remainder, vs = −qv + g(s, v), (7.2) with input in a sufficiently small disk about zero. Ordinary parameters may occur analytically in all the displayed data. The estimates hold for every fixed number of independent retained-free and ordinary derivatives, and for the controlled input tests of Assumption 4.2. No exceptional unsafe-column loss is required. For each fixed finite request the estimates have uniform constants and far-regime thresholds on the controlled families of Definition 4.1, independently of the individual tests’ return times to the ordinary germ. This primitive library is retestable for elimination in the sense of Definition 5.6, with its fixed local sector determinations.
